final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced at 495e1d30 (Go 1.24.4, 8 cores).

**Expected:** Running separate `cli.Command`s in parallel goroutines (default `HelpFlag`, no `HideHelp`) does not panic.
**Actual:** `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`, same as the report. It shows up in the first second or so of the 100000-count run: 4 of 4 runs failed, after 0.04 to 0.6 s. The stack:
`boolValue.Get` (flag_bool.go:71, `*b.destination`) ← `FlagBase.Get` ← `Command.Value` ← `Command.Bool` ← `checkHelp` (command.go:186) ← `Command.run` (command_run.go:198).
`go test -race` also reports DATA RACEs within 200 iterations.
**Trigger:** Two goroutines each running `Command.Run` at the same time. Each one's `setupDefaults` resets the single package-global `HelpFlag` (`applied=false`, `value=nil`, see the "TODO need to remove hack" in command_setup.go:202-210) and then applies it again. Meanwhile the other goroutine's `checkHelp` reads that same flag's value through a `boolValue` whose `destination` hasn't been set yet.
**Run:** `go test ./repro/ -count 100000 -failfast`
**Artifacts:** `repro/debug_test.go` is the reporter's test as written. I only renamed the package and added a stack dump to the recover message. No production code was changed.

Setup note: `git fetch` from github.com was blocked on this machine, so I pulled the same commit as a tarball from codeload.github.com and made a local base commit for the diff.
